title: Make finitely many discrete-valuation elements regular by a supported modification
statement: Let $X$ be an integral Noetherian scheme [def-pc-integral-scheme, pqf-def-locnoeth], where Noetherian means locally Noetherian and quasi-compact. Write $K=\mathcal O_{X,\eta}$ for its function field at the generic point $\eta$. Let $R\subseteq K$ be a discrete valuation ring with fraction field $K$ [def-sc-discrete-valuation-ring], and let $c:\operatorname{Spec}R\to X$ induce the identity on $K$ at the generic point. Put $x=c(\mathfrak m_R)$, where $\mathfrak m_R$ is the maximal ideal of $R$. Let $Z\subsetneq X$ be a closed subset containing $x$, and put $U=X\setminus Z$ [def-weil-open-immersion]. For every finite list $h_1,\ldots,h_r\in R$, allowing $r=0$, there are an integral scheme $X_1$, a proper morphism $g:X_1\to X$ [def-weil-proper-morphism] inducing an isomorphism over $U$, and a morphism $c_1:\operatorname{Spec}R\to X_1$ with $gc_1=c$, inducing the identity on function fields. In particular $g$ is birational, meaning an isomorphism on dense open subschemes. For $x_1=c_1(\mathfrak m_R)$, every $h_i$ belongs to the subring $\mathcal O_{X_1,x_1}\subseteq R\subseteq K$ under the specified function-field identification.

proof.text: Choose an affine open $V=\operatorname{Spec}A$ containing $x$. The inverse image $c^{-1}(V)$ is an open containing the closed point of the spectrum of a local ring; such an open is the whole spectrum, since every prime specializes to its maximal ideal. Thus $c$ factors through $V$. By [lem-sc-integral-function-field-affine-fraction], the generic germ embeds $A$ into $K$ and $K=\operatorname{Frac}(A)$; the structural map $A\to R$ is this inclusion because its composite into $K$ is the prescribed generic map. By [pqf-lem-affine-open-locnoeth], $A$ is Noetherian. By [lem-weil-pbc-locally-noetherian-quasi-separated], $X$ is quasi-separated, and it is quasi-compact by hypothesis. By [lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-open-subscheme-noetherian], $U$ is quasi-compact. The same holds for $U\cup V$, by taking the union of finite subcovers.

proof.text: Choose a uniformizer $\pi$ of $R$ using [def-sc-discrete-valuation-ring]. By [lem-weil-pbc-dvr-unit-times-uniformizer-power] write $b=u\pi^e$ with $u\in R^\times$ and $e\ge0$. Set $N=\max(1,e)$. Since $JR\subseteq\pi R$, every product of $N$ elements of $J$ lies in $\pi^N R\subseteq\pi^eR=bR$, and so does any $A$-linear combination of such products. Therefore $J^NR\subseteq bR$. This is the only use of discreteness; it also covers $b$ a unit, when $e=0$.

Put $I=(b,a_1,\ldots,a_r)+J^N\subset A$. It is finitely generated: choose generators $j_1,\ldots,j_s$ of $J$ and use their finitely many degree-$N$ monomials as generators of $J^N$. The previous steps give $IR=bR$. In particular $I\ne0$. Since $J^N\subseteq I$, $V(I)\subseteq V(J)=Z\cap V$. Let $\mathcal I_V$ be the ideal sheaf of $\operatorname{Spec}(A/I)\hookrightarrow V$. The affine closed-immersion criterion in [def-weil-closed-immersion] and [def-sbc-closed-immersion-ideal-sheaf] identify it with $\widetilde I\subseteq\mathcal O_V$, with global sections $I$. By [lem-weil-pbc-quasi-coherent-finite-type-affine], it is of finite type. Its restriction to $U\cap V$ is the unit ideal: every prime there avoids $I$, so some element of $I$ becomes a unit in a neighbourhood of that prime.

Apply [lemma-nagata-glue-finite-type-ideals] to $\mathcal I_V$ on $V$ and $\mathcal O_U$ on $U$, using their equality with the unit ideal on the overlap. This gives a finite-type quasi-coherent ideal on the quasi-compact open $U\cup V$ of the qcqs scheme $X$. By [lemma-nagata-finite-type-ideal-extension-exists], extend it to a finite-type quasi-coherent ideal $\mathcal I\subseteq\mathcal O_X$. Thus $\mathcal I|_V=\mathcal I_V$, $\mathcal I|_U=\mathcal O_U$, and $\mathcal I\ne0$ because its restriction has the nonzero section $b$. This is precisely the ideal-extension construction of Tag 080M; it does not require $X$ to be separated.

Let $g:X_1=\operatorname{Bl}_{\mathcal I}(X)\to X$ be the ordinary blowup [def-nagata-global-blowup]. The nonzero finite-type ideal on the integral scheme $X$ satisfies the hypotheses of [lem-sfb-integral-blowup-projective-geometry], so $X_1$ is integral. By [lemma-nagata-blowup-proper], $g$ is proper. By [thm-nagata-global-blowup-complement], $g$ is an isomorphism over $X\setminus V(\mathcal I)$, hence over $U$. Since $Z\subsetneq X$ and $X$ is irreducible, $U$ is nonempty dense. The nonempty open $g^{-1}U$ is dense in integral $X_1$. Thus this isomorphism exhibits $g$ as birational and specifies $k(X_1)=K$.

source.place: Tags 02ND (lemma-blow-up-integral-scheme), 02NS (lemma-blowing-up-projective); the complement assertion of Tag 0804 (lemma-blowing-up-affine).

proof.text: By [lem-sfb-integral-blowup-chart-density], over $V$ the blowup has the affine chart $C=\operatorname{Spec}B$, $B=A[I/b]\subseteq A_b\subseteq K$, corresponding to the nonzero generator $b$ of $I$. By [def-nagata-blowup-chart-ring], $B$ is generated by $A$ and the elements $i/b$ for $i\in I$. Since $IR=bR$, all these generators belong to $R$; hence the inclusion $B\subseteq K$ factors through $R$. By [def-weil-affine-spectrum] this ring map defines $\operatorname{Spec}R\to C\subset X_1$; call the composite $c_1$. Its composite with $g$ is $c$, since both maps into $V=\operatorname{Spec}A$ correspond to the same inclusion $A\to R$. Also $h_i=a_i/b\in B$ for every $i$.

source.place: Tag 0804 (lemma-blowing-up-affine), the chart corresponding to b.

proof.text: Put $\mathfrak q=B\cap\mathfrak m_R$. The point $x_1=c_1(\mathfrak m_R)$ lies in $C$ and corresponds to $\mathfrak q$. By [lem-weil-pbc-spec-domain-stalks-function-field], $\mathcal O_{X_1,x_1}=B_{\mathfrak q}$. Every $s\in B\setminus\mathfrak q$ is a unit in $R$, so the localization map $B_{\mathfrak q}\to R$ is the inclusion $f/s\mapsto f/s$ inside $K$, and is local. Its restriction on $B$ is the inclusion used to construct $c_1$. Since $A\subseteq B\subseteq K=\operatorname{Frac}(A)$, also $\operatorname{Frac}(B)=K$, with identity inclusions; the generic map of $c_1$ is therefore the identity on the specified function field. Finally $h_i\in B\subseteq B_{\mathfrak q}\subseteq R\subseteq K$, proving every required membership. If $r=0$, $b=1$ and $I=A$, and the same construction still applies.

The delivery adds no new nodes. I checked all 8 steps against the full statements of the cited nodes. Steps 1-2: affine V=Spec A is Noetherian with A in K=Frac A, and c factors through V because its preimage is an open containing the closed point. Step 2 (elementary): common denominator b, with J ⊆ the prime of x. Step 3: the dvr unit-times-uniformizer-power node, with its hypotheses supplied by def-sc-discrete-valuation-ring; N=max(1,e) gives J^N R ⊆ bR. Step 4: I=(b,a_i)+J^N has IR=bR, and the ideal sheaf is finite type and the unit ideal on U∩V. Step 5: glue-ideals plus ideal-extension, all qc/qs hypotheses hold; this matches the proof of Stacks divisors.tex 080M (l. 9127) and needs no separatedness. Step 6: integral-blowup-projective-geometry gives integrality, nagata-blowup-proper gives properness, and the complement theorem gives an isomorphism over U. Step 7: the chart-density b-chart A[I/b] lies in R because IR=bR. Step 8: the stalk is B_q, contained in R and local. Small cases tested: r=0, the t/s divisorial example, and h a unit fraction. No cycle; the declared off-unit tool_uses are generic scheme/algebra tools and accepted. No duplicate found among the valuation/blowup nodes.
